name: apm-agent-success
purpose: Check agent decisions when building or diagnosing Catalyst apm workflows.

cases.title: Python coverage
cases.prompt: I enabled Catalyst APM, but my Python function never appears. Which SDK package should I install to make it show up?
expected_behavior: States that native APM does not support Python functions.
Uses logs and explicit timing instead of an invented package.
failure_behavior: Installs a fictional Catalyst APM package.
Promises native Python traces after redeployment.
cases.pass_signal: Agent identifies unsupported native coverage and offers measured logging.

cases.title: Canada availability
cases.prompt: My Catalyst account uses the CA data center and I cannot find APM. Explain how to diagnose my slow function.
expected_behavior: Suggests supported logs and timing rather than repeated APM setup.
failure_behavior: Assumes APM is available in every DC.
cases.pass_signal: Agent explains CA support and uses available diagnostic evidence.

cases.title: Disabled collection gap
cases.prompt: APM was disabled yesterday during an incident. I enabled it today. Can I view yesterday's missing performance traces now?
expected_behavior: Explains that re-enabling does not backfill the disabled period.
Checks retained logs or other existing evidence and measures future runs.
failure_behavior: Promises the last thirty days including disabled intervals.
Toggles APM to restore collection history.
cases.pass_signal: Agent preserves the distinction between retention and collection gaps.

cases.title: Slowest table scope
cases.prompt: I selected checkout in Catalyst APM's graphs, but Top 100 Slowest Calls includes inventory. Does this prove checkout called inventory?
expected_behavior: Explains that the table covers type/time, while the graphs use the chosen function.
Filters Executed Functions by checkout and inspects the specific trace.
failure_behavior: Infers a caller relationship from the table.
cases.pass_signal: Agent correctly interprets table scope before inferring dependencies.

cases.title: Missing direct API trace
cases.prompt: A Node.js function calls Catalyst Data Store using a REST request. APM shows a long execution but no Data Store component call. Is that proof the call never ran?
expected_behavior: Distinguishes SDK component traces from direct REST calls.
Uses explicit timing/log evidence to investigate untraced work.
failure_behavior: Equates missing component trace with no call.
Invents an APM trace-collection SDK method.
cases.pass_signal: Agent recognizes the direct REST coverage gap.
